verdict: These are the same caret drawn twice — 3×36 CSS px, #00B5FF, hard-edged, no selection in either — and B lost on the one thing that moved: it took the font's ascent/descent line box literally and never corrected for it, so 10.5px of bare cyan hangs above the x-height while only 7px reaches under the 'p' of 'steps'. A nudged it 1px down and its centre lands within half a pixel of the ink centre; that is the difference between a caret that straddles the letters and one that hovers over them. Neither earns the word 'alive': a 3px-wide, full-leading slab in the loudest saturated cyan on a #F9F9F9 page is a code-editor cursor wearing a novelist's typeface, and with no selection state visible in either shot half of this component is simply unjudgeable.

states.name: selection
states.gap: B's caret starts 3 device px (1.5 CSS px) right of the selection's trailing edge - fill ends at 1403, caret occupies 1407-1412 instead of flush at the 1404 character seam - leaving a visible hairline of #F9F9F9 paper between highlight and caret and putting the caret's centre ~2.75 CSS px past the true insertion offset (A's caret lands exactly on the 25.33px monospace advance boundary).
states.gapTheirs: A draws a second, pixel-identical 6px x 72px #00B5FF bar at the LEFT edge of the selection (x 942-947) as well as the right (x 1404-1409) - two indistinguishable carets, so nothing on screen tells the writer which end is live and which way shift-arrow will extend; the left bar sits outside the fill (fill starts at 948), confirming it is a decorative outline rule, not an anchor.
states.verdict: A turns the selection into a bracketed chip: two identical bright bars, one at each end, so the caret stops being a caret and becomes packaging. The instant you shift-arrow you are guessing which end moves, and that guess is the whole point of a caret. B has one bar, in the right place conceptually, and pays for it with a 1.5px sliver of paper between highlight and caret that a typographer will see on every selection and never unsee - a registration error, but a survivable one. Ambiguity about where the cursor is beats a hairline gap every time; B wins on the one thing that matters here.

states.name: unfocused
states.gap: Caret box is misaligned with its own line box by 3 device px (~1.5 CSS px): it leaves 21px of headroom above the ascender tops but only 14px below the descender bottoms — a 1.5:1 top/bottom imbalance, versus B's 19px/16px (1.19:1). A's caret centre sits 3.5px above the glyph ink centre; B's sits 1.5px above. The caret visibly rides high, belonging to the line above rather than to the word it is inserting into.
states.gapTheirs: Caret sits 1 device px further right than A's: 7px clear of the 's' terminal in 'steps' vs A's 6px, putting its centre 5.5px past the monospace cell boundary vs A's 4.5px. On a fixed-width grid where every advance is 26px, that reads as a hair of slack between the caret and the word it is attached to.
states.verdict: These are the same caret: 6 device px wide (3 CSS px), 72px tall, #AFE5FB vs #AEE5FB, hard square ends, no rounding, no selection rendered anywhere in either frame. B wins only because its blade is seated in the line box within 1px of centre while A's floats 3px high — a real but small thing, the kind you feel as vague wrongness after an hour rather than see at once. Both are guilty of the same disqualifying error: a caret at 1.29:1 against #F9F9F9 while the text runs 16.19:1, so the one element that must never be lost is the palest thing on the page, and at 3px wide it reads as a smear of highlighter, not a blade you can aim.
